issues.description: The problem statement requires a public method named checkOrderReady() on SealSaloon (used in the task description and UML). The provided solution implements the order-serving logic in a method named processOrders() instead and does not provide a checkOrderReady() method. This name mismatch between the specification and the solution can confuse students about which method name to implement and test against.
issues.suggestedFix: Either rename the solution's processOrders() method to checkOrderReady(), or add a public checkOrderReady() method that delegates to processOrders(). Update any documentation or UML to consistently use the same method name so students know which method to implement.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML expect a method named checkOrderReady() on SealSaloon, but the solution implements and calls a method named processOrders() for the same functionality. This mismatch between the expected API (checkOrderReady) and the implemented identifier (processOrders) creates a mapping barrier for students: they will look for checkOrderReady() in the provided solution/template but find a differently named method, increasing extraneous cognitive load and potentially causing confusion when matching requirements to implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename processOrders() in SealSaloon to checkOrderReady(), or add a public checkOrderReady() method that delegates to processOrders(). This aligns the implementation with the problem statement and UML, removing the identifier mismatch while preserving behavior.
